explanation: This method treats the requested object and destination as runtime visual identities. It measures the package, its supporting table, and the bowl from current RGB-D rather than using image coordinates as a trajectory. It fits the package top and table planes, intersects identified visible top corners with the measured top plane, and fits the bowl opening from measured rim samples. The grasp uses the actual pad offset, opening axis, and finger envelope; visual straddling is checked before descent. A textured reference and persistent printed-landmark definitions are acquired before contact. Retention requires independently observed package motion matching measured hand motion during an actual lift. Unknown registration invokes current corresponding-landmark measurements, with one justified view-changing action if needed. Transfer uses bounded, locally reviewed feedback legs, not an unavailable collision certificate. Release occurs above the rim with the fingers above it, followed by withdrawal and two fresh observations of the actual supported relation and stability. Historical geometry and contact-phase evidence are checkpointed for repairs. Missing evidence, failed registration, stalls, insufficient clearance, or exhausted reserves produce an explicit incomplete result without reopening an uncertain held load.
interface: Entry point: main(api). The task text is runtime data from this request; all identities, pixels, geometry, grasp alignment, and motion endpoints are acquired or calculated during the episode. The method uses only the published state, review, point/region measurements, plane_point, camera, tracker, compose, drive, control, checkpoint, recall, and note interfaces. All review calls declare exact structured fields, explicit unknown outcomes, and supported named measurements. Failed measurements are logged and dictionary membership is checked before use. Geometry uses geo.plane.coefficients, geo.circle_xy, geo.rotation, geo.pad_position, geo.transform, and geo.attachment_error. Source constants are bounded controller settings, uncertainty allowances, and local observation-action distances, not a stored trajectory. A drive lease has at most 14 calls; route loops have at most 16 legs of at most 85 mm, with one view-only correction. A registration recovery has at most two reviews and one justified view displacement. Initial acquisition has at most two attempts. The method reserves 18 Jev decisions until release, reports numerical failed-clearance and retention evidence, and never treats drive convergence as object evidence. Checkpoints retain compact reference geometry, persistent landmark identities, pending contact phases, lift baselines, retention observations, and final observation provenance. Tracker handles are never restored after repair. Return value is JSON-compatible with completion_proposed and evidence. Incomplete execution preserves the physical state and reports the exact unresolved dependency.
jev_protocol: Every physical update is dispatched through api.control, directly for gripper transitions or indirectly through api.drive for bounded pose feedback. Each call supplies exactly x, y, z, rx, ry, rz and gripper choice questions. Each axis question explicitly names its subject and the bound processed_features.axes.<axis>.goal_relation selector. Jev chooses positive for increase, negative for decrease, and hold for within_tolerance; rotations use the published world rotation-vector sign and xyzw orientation convention. The host computes residual magnitudes, deadbands, L2 limits and pad-center-to-TCP conversion from current proprioception, then dispatches Jev's answers unchanged. The gripper question explicitly selects open, close or keep from processed_features.objective.gripper. Program features label the current phase and measurement provenance, not an invented object sensor. Program code, not Jev, computes plane fits, rim clearance, rotations, finger-height margins, registration uncertainty, hand/object displacement, and attachment errors. Image review supplies visual identities, named point/region requests, persistent landmark definitions, current contact/release interpretations, and explicit obstruction/visibility outcomes. none_seen is not certified clearance; partial or self occlusion can permit justified bounded local progress, while an observed obstacle stops motion. A requested view change must identify a specific missing feature and a locally justified finite direction. Registration is accepted only with adequate measured support or independently observed corresponding physical landmarks. Retention additionally requires an actual upward package displacement consistent with actual hand displacement. A reached receipt establishes only robot convergence and command delivery; moved is accepted only in the gripper hold transition, stalled stops, and lease_exhausted requires substantial measured progress before another bounded route leg. Final completion is proposed only after observed release, actual supported containment, and agreement between two post-release physical-landmark observations; it is not official success.
